findings.title: The nonlocal inner products and coercivity fail in the admitted two-dimensional zero-parameter case
findings.core_impact: The inner products used to define boundary adjoints and invoke Hilbert-complex Fredholm/kernel theory do not exist as asserted on the whole stated parameter/domain range.
findings.repair_boundary: Restrict the low-dimensional zero case or supply capacity/charge-normalized spaces and new proofs. For lambda>0, use a global M energy identity, start with the unsquared dual norm, bound it by the energy norm through a bounded trace lifting and Gaffney equivalence, and square only at the end. No claim is made that N>=3 zero-parameter coercivity is false.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The admitted Euclidean N=2, lambda=0 case includes a circular constant density. Its logarithmic potential has boundary value R(2*pi*c-log R), so the proposed quadratic form is zero at R=exp(2*pi*c) and negative above it. The exterior Dirichlet integral grows as 2*pi*R^2*log(T/R), invalidating the finite whole-space energy step. This falsifies the stated inner-product/coercivity scope used for adjoints, not just a normalization convention.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The positive-parameter theory and compact-manifold restriction do not remove the explicitly admitted Euclidean zero case. No failure in N>=3 is inferred.
independent_verification.repair_check: Positive lambda restores the energy comparison after correcting the unsquared dual norm and global lifting; a zero-parameter capacity/charge restriction needs a separately valid theorem.

findings.title: The zero-frequency compatibility conditions are vacuous because the two kernels are interchanged
findings.core_impact: The stated solvability criterion for the original zero-frequency BVPs is false, and it is explicitly used in the boundary/domain comparison. This is substantive despite the short kernel-label correction.
findings.repair_boundary: Interchange the kernels in (2.5), propagate the corrected compatibility requirement, and replace nV by tV on the right of (2.9b), consistent with (2.8b). Retain nonzero-kappa conclusions separately.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The actual p9 definitions force nV=0 in ker D_n and tV=0 in ker D_t, making both tests automatic. On the disk at kappa=0, degree-two component of DU=0 gives dU1=0 and Stokes forbids tU1=dtheta; degree-zero gives delta U1=0 and forbids constant nonzero normal flux. All prescribed data are smooth in the stated trace spaces.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: An augmented harmonic-multiplier problem is different from the original homogeneous equation; nonzero kappa is not refuted.
independent_verification.repair_check: Swap the kernels and correct (2.9b)'s test trace; the substantive solvability criterion changes despite the short edit.

findings.title: The mixed Hodge–Laplace representation has reversed boundary signs
locations: PDF23/printed22, general representation and Calderon scheme
PDF29/printed28, displayed normal jump of SL[Delta]
findings.core_impact: A central representation proposition is false for smooth data in the favorable positive-parameter regime. The BVP-to-Calderon derivation cannot consistently use the printed formula and the declared potential/jump conventions.
findings.repair_boundary: Reverse the two boundary signs in Proposition4.6 and its proof, keep the PDF33 potential definitions, and recheck the resulting Calderon equations. Correct the PDF29 normal jump to -Id. The formal weak Hodge structure of the defined BIOs is not refuted by this example.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: I inspected the actual grouped formula on PDF32. With N=3, lambda=1, ell=1, U=(chi_ball,0), its piecewise mixed equation has F=(-chi_ball,0) and all separate graph traces. The fixed exterior-minus-interior jump is -1. Distributionally P=-dq and delta P=q-chi_ball, so the printed matrix applied to (-q,+P) gives 2q-chi_ball; at r=2 it equals exp(-3), whereas U0=0. The outer common factor is present and is not the defect.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: Correct surrounding weak forms do not validate this sign-dependent representation. No assertion is made that every positive-parameter BIO theorem fails.
independent_verification.repair_check: Changing the boundary signs to -SL[Tn]+DL[Tt] recovers the example and the distributional source-vector calculation; propagate the fixed jump convention.

findings.title: The Newton-potential target in (3.3) incorrectly includes second-order graph regularity across its source
findings.core_impact: The displayed mapping assertion is false, but the extra across-source regularity is unnecessary for the intended sidewise boundary-potential calculus.
findings.repair_boundary: Retain H1_loc globally; assert second-order graph regularity only away from the source or with stronger input. Derive sidewise graph regularity for the actual trace densities as above. This explicit repair preserves the intended potential operators; it does not by itself repair F1 or F3.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: In one dimension delta0 lies in H^-1_comp but the Yukawa fundamental solution (1/2)exp(-|x|) has second derivative equal to itself minus delta0, hence not L2_loc. The global second-order graph claim is false.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: PDF19 already states the sidewise homogeneous mapping required for layer potentials; the valid H1_loc mapping and commutation suffice for the intended graph-density calculus. The erroneous strengthening is not an essential core premise.
independent_verification.repair_check: Remove across-source second-order regularity or strengthen the source class. Retain sidewise graph regularity on the declared densities.

findings.title: The representation hypotheses do not imply the componentwise graph traces used in their proofs
findings.core_impact: The general propositions overstate their domain. The BVP applications can be confined to the componentwise graph domains already specified earlier.
findings.repair_boundary: Require appropriate piecewise H Lambda(D) in Proposition4.3 and H Lambda^ell(Delta) in Proposition4.5; this is the regularity used by the displayed Green identities. Alternatively build the larger maximal-domain trace theory explicitly. Restricting to the already-declared BVP domains closes this specific issue; it does not remove F3, whose example is regular.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: For f=sum k^-1/2 z^k, orthogonality gives finite scalar L2 norm and infinite gradient energy. Cauchy-Riemann gives delta(-w dxdy)=-du, so U=u-w dxdy is a compactly supported piecewise L2 solution of DU=0 while dU and delta U are not separately L2. It fails the componentwise graph traces claimed for the broad proposition.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: PDF24 explicitly gives the intended BVP domain H Lambda(D) and Green identity on it. Restricting the proposition to that already-stated domain preserves the intended application; maximal weak traces are not denied.
independent_verification.repair_check: Require piecewise componentwise graph domains or develop a larger maximal-domain trace theory. This does not repair F3, whose example already has regular traces.

findings.title: Several displayed operators have incompatible degree labels
findings.core_impact: The literal displayed matrices and some domain specifications are not well-defined with the stated grading.
findings.repair_boundary: Correct the degree labels consistently in formulas and figures. For corrected W, the Schur complement is -(d_(l-1)d_(l-1)^*+d_l^*d_l+lambda*I), preserving the claimed positive-parameter Hodge–Laplace structure. Full-star and atomic-potential corrections follow uniquely from the definitions.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The types d_j:Lambda^j->Lambda^(j+1), delta_j:Lambda^j->Lambda^(j-1) and star_j:Lambda^j->Lambda^(N-j) determine the corrected indices. In particular -d_(ell-1)^* is needed in the upper-right block.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: I read PDF31's correct weak form (4.15): -(g_ell,d_(ell-1)v_(ell-1)) already supplies the valid adjoint coupling independently of the incorrectly labelled matrix. Thus an existing valid derivation bypasses the display errors.
independent_verification.repair_check: Propagate the degree corrections through equations and figures; the correctly typed Schur complement is the expected negative shifted Hodge-Laplacian.
